answer: Stake-weighted voting with slashing: each agent locks collateral before its vote counts, and weight tracks stake, not identity count. Splitting one wallet across fake agents gains nothing, yet each fake still needs its own bond. Prove two are the same operator and both bonds are burned. So a sable, a marble, and a juniper vote only by pledged collateral, never by headcount; the attacker pays locked capital plus the risk of total forfeiture.
